sections.h2: Which sale method gets a Centerville, Ohio house closed fastest?
sections.html:
Cash gets you to the closing table fastest, while a listing generally earns more. Centerville is a core suburb of the Dayton area, so a house in good order can draw buyers on the open market.

  • Agent listing: suited to a maintained house in a sought-after school zone. Plan on staging, showings, and a buyer's inspection.
  • As-is cash sale: sensible when the roof, the mechanicals, or the finishes need money you would rather not spend before selling.
  • Private sale: an option when a buyer is already in hand. A written contract and a title company still protect both sides.

Census figures show 85.3% of residents stayed in their house through the previous year, so most sellers here know the property well and can answer a buyer's questions.

sections.h2: What do Centerville's housing statistics look like?
sections.html:
Centerville skews older and owner-occupied. In 2020 the census found a median age of 48.8. Residents 65 and over made up 29.5% of the population, and owners held 70.4% of occupied homes. The mid-2025 estimate of 25,194 residents sits 4.2% above the 2020 base the Census Bureau uses.

sections.h2: When was Centerville settled, and does its age affect my sale?
sections.html:
Three brothers-in-law surveyed the area in February 1796, two months before Dayton was established. The state recognized Centerville in 1803, it was platted in 1805, and it was reached town status in 1830. It became a city on December 2, 1968, and the post office changed the spelling from Centreville to Centerville in 1900.

Early settlers built log houses and then limestone ones. Wikipedia says nearly 100 stone buildings stood along local streets in the nineteenth century, many survive, and the city holds the largest collection of early stone houses in Ohio. For a house in the historic core near the Heart of Centerville, ask the city whether review rules cover exterior changes before offering a buyer a renovation.

Away from the old center, suburban growth filled in the map. School enrollment passed 6,800 in 1969, and Centerville High School moved to its present campus in 1973, which hints at when much of the city was built.

sections.h2: How does a Centerville deed reach the Montgomery County record?
sections.html:
Part of Centerville extends into Greene County, so look at your tax bill to see which county applies. For most Centerville parcels the deed goes through Montgomery County's Auditor, whose Deed Transfer Department adds a transfer or no-transfer stamp, and then to the Recorder.

The Recorder's FAQ says a deed needs the names of buyer and seller, the legal description, the seller's signature, and a notary block. It says documents are recorded the same business day they arrive, once the Auditor has stamped them. Items that need a No Transfer stamp, such as transfer on death designations and easements, are mailed or walked through the Auditor's department. Recording fees change, so get the schedule from the Recorder first.

  • Under Revised Code 319.202, the transfer fee is a seller cost.
  • Paying off a mortgage creates no new deed. The lender records a release, viewable on the county's online records search.
  • The county holds roughly 230,000 parcels, so quote your parcel number on every form.

sections.h2: What is the process for disputing a Centerville property value?
sections.html:
The Montgomery County Board of Revision opens its filing period on January 1 and closes it at the end of March. Each complaint must state the value you want and your reasoning. Under Revised Code 5715.19 the date can run later when first-half collection closes after March 31.

The person who files must prove the case. The county lists acceptable evidence as a sale of the property within three years, a recent appraisal, sales of similar nearby homes, a realtor's market analysis, and itemized repair estimates. Lists of other properties' assessed values, comments on neighbors' upkeep, and tax rate complaints do not count.

Tax year 2025 hearings ran by video or phone and lasted 10 to 20 minutes per property. The board mails a decision within 90 days. Either side then has 30 days to go to the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals or the county Court of Common Pleas. A changed value holds until the next countywide update, which comes every three years unless the property is rebuilt or damaged.

sections.h2: What does Ohio's condition disclosure form require of a Centerville seller?
sections.html:
Revised Code 5302.30 asks sellers of buildings of up to four dwellings to describe the water supply, sewage system, roof, foundation, walls, floors, and known hazards on a state form. A buyer who first receives it after signing the contract can back out within three business days.

Transfers by an estate fiduciary, between spouses, to a lineal relative, or by an heir who did not live in the home the previous year are exempt. Centerville is prone to tornadoes, floods, and severe storms according to Wikipedia, so tell a buyer about any storm or water damage you know of.

sections.h2: What is the story behind Centerville's schools and old houses?
sections.html:
Centerville schools enrolled about 550 students in 1863 and stayed in the hundreds until 1955, when the count passed 1,100. By 1969 more than 6,800 students attended, and the district took the name Centerville City Schools that year. Elementary buildings date from 1955 through 2007, among them Weller, Stingley, Driscoll, Normandy, Cline, and John Hole, and the three middle schools are Magsig, Watts, and Tower Heights.

The town also has an Underground Railroad past. Wikipedia reports evidence of four safe houses in Centerville and Washington Township. The Town Hall Theatre was built in 1908 as the township hall and became a performing arts center in 1989. In 2008 voters considered a merger commission with Washington Township, which passed in the city and failed in the township.

sections.h2: Which schools, hospitals, and amenities draw buyers to Centerville?
sections.html:
In all, the district operates two primary schools, six elementary schools, three middle schools, one high school, and an alternative high school. The Washington-Centerville Public Library lists more than 380,000 items.

Miami Valley Hospital South opened in 2007 as an outpatient site with an emergency department and grew into a full hospital with 60 beds by 2013, on a campus beside Interstate 675. Wikipedia calls it the city's largest employer and lists retail and health care as the top job categories. The council-manager government has a seven-member council elected at large, and the Town Hall Theatre downtown dates to 1908. For 2022 the Census shows retail sales of $44,802 per resident.

faqs.q: Which county handles my Centerville sale?
faqs.a: Mostly Montgomery County, with a small portion of the city in Greene County. The county on your deed and tax bill has the auditor, treasurer, and recorder who process your paperwork.

faqs.q: Does a historic stone house in Centerville need a review before I sell?
faqs.a: Ask the city's planning and zoning office whether your address falls in a historic area with review rules. Settle that question before offering a buyer exterior changes.

faqs.q: Who bears the transfer fee on a Centerville house?
faqs.a: The seller. It lands on the seller under Revised Code 319.202, and the closing statement itemizes it.

faqs.q: When can Montgomery County owners file a value complaint?
faqs.a: Filing opens on New Year's Day and closes March 31. Upload your market value evidence to the county portal ten days or more ahead of the hearing.

faqs.q: Do I fill out the disclosure form for an inherited Centerville house?
faqs.a: Often not. The disclosure statute, Revised Code 5302.30, excludes estate fiduciaries and heirs who never occupied the home in the prior year. If you lived there, complete it. Your closing agent can say which case fits you.
